metadata.title: Innovative Approaches for Nonprescription Drug Products
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 31 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 32 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 33 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 34 not required. 35
candidates.context: These innovative approaches may be useful for applicants intending to develop and seek 26 approval of certain nonprescription drug products through the submission of a new drug 27 application (NDA), including an application submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the 28 Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (21 U.S.C. 355). 2 1 This guidance has been prepared by the Office of Medical Policy in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research at the Food and Drug Administration at the Food and Drug Administration.

candidates.statement: FDA approves new drugs 3 as prescription or nonprescription drug products under section 505 of 40 the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 355). A drug product must be dispensed by prescription if it is not 41 safe to use except under the supervision of a practitioner licensed by law to administer the drug 42 ( health care practitioner ) (see section 503(b)(1) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 353(b)(1)). If a 43 drug product does not meet the criteria for prescription-only dispensing, it may be marketed as a 44 nonprescription drug product. 45
candidates.context: FDA determines whether the information submitted as part of a new drug application (NDA) for 47 a nonprescription drug product is sufficient to ensure that the drug product is safe and effective 48 for nonprescription use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in its 49 proposed labeling (see sections 505(d) and 503(b)(1) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 355(d) and 50 353(b)(1)). Studies regarding self-selection and actual use can help demonstrate that the drug 51 product is safe and effective for use without the supervision of a health care practitioner. Self- 52 selection studies test whether consumers can apply information in the drug product’s labeling to 53 their personal medical situations and make correct decisions to use or not use the drug product, 54 and actual use studies provide information on how consumers will use the drug product. 4

candidates.statement: Nonprescription drug products must comply with applicable labeling requirements for over-the- 57 counter (OTC) drug products under 21 CFR part 201, including, but not limited to, the format 58 and content requirements for OTC drug product labeling under § 201.66. Labeling created to 59 satisfy the requirements in § 201.66 is commonly referred to as the DFL. The DFL is intended to 60 enable consumers to appropriately self-select and use the nonprescription drug product safely 61 and effectively. In instances where the DFL alone would not be sufficient, an applicant may 62 consider proposing innovative approaches, in addition to the DFL, to ensure that the drug 63 product is safe and effective for use as a nonprescription drug product. 64

Nonprescription Drug Products With Additional Conditions for Safe and 93 Effective Use 94 Examples of additional conditions for safe and effective use that the Agency may consider, 100 particularly with regard to appropriate self-selection and actual use, include, but are not limited 101 to, the following: 102

candidates.statement:  Prior to purchase, the consumer is required to respond to a set of questions on a self- 104 selection test in a mobile application, and the outcome of the self-selection test 105 affirmatively indicates that the consumer is an appropriate candidate to use the 106 nonprescription drug product. 107
